children: Employees at C3A grade and above will receive no quarterly variable allowance after TCS fell short of internal performance targets, while junior staff remain eligible for full payouts

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) will withhold quarterly variable pay for employees at the C3A grade and above for the September quarter, following a shortfall against internal performance targets, according to an internal memo reported by Reuters.

In the memo, Sudeep Kunnumal, Chief Human Resources Officer at TCS, said the decision had been taken after the company’s performance fell short of internal expectations. Employees in the affected grades typically include professionals with seven to 10 years of experience through to senior-level management.

Junior-level employees, however, will receive 100 per cent of their eligible quarterly variable allowance, the report said. Employees who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity said TCS typically paid between 50 and 100 per cent of variable pay, making this the first time in at least two years that the company had explicitly announced a complete withholding for the affected group.

The decision comes amid pressure on traditional IT services demand. TCS reported its weakest sequential revenue growth for a September quarter in three years, even as its annualised artificial intelligence revenue rose nearly 20 per cent, according to Reuters. The company’s shares rose as much as 6.2 per cent on Friday following its results, with investors responding positively to the growth in AI-related business.

TCS reported consolidated revenue of US$7.64 billion for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, up 2.4 per cent year on year in US dollar terms and 0.2 per cent sequentially. Its annualised AI revenue crossed US$3 billion, while its workforce stood at 598,056 at the end of the quarter.
